多數人以為信仰要處理的是「行為」——少說謊、多做好事。但聖經的診斷更深：問題出在:
Most people assume faith is about behaviour — fewer lies, more good deeds. The Bible's diagnosis goes deeper: the trouble is in the root, not the fruit.
Our fundamental problem is self — making myself the centre of everything, insisting on being my own master and king, wanting to take God's place. That is pride: leaving the position of a man and seizing the authority of God. Adam and Eve did not eat that fruit because they were hungry; they ate it to “be like God, knowing good and evil.”
The moment self comes in, four cracks open at once: man is cut off from God, man is at odds with himself, people wound one another, and man's world falls out of order. Nearly every trouble you and I carry can be traced to one of those four cracks.
So the gospel's real question is not “what wrong have you done?” but “who has been reigning over your life?”

耶穌不是一個宗教創辦人。祂是一個歷史人物，有確切的年代、地點與見證人。祂做了三件:
Jesus is not the founder of a religion. He is a figure of history, with a definite date, a definite place, and eyewitnesses. He did three things nobody else would dare: He forgave sins, He accepted worship, and He said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.”
Faced with a claim like that, there are only three possibilities: He was a liar, He was a madman, or He really is Lord. His character and His life rule out the first two — a liar does not get crucified for his lie, and a madman does not deliver the Sermon on the Mount.
His death and resurrection rest on solid historical ground: an empty tomb, more than five hundred witnesses, disciples who went from running away to dying as martyrs. No one dies for something he knows to be false.

Every religion in the world teaches people how to climb up to God. Only the gospel says God came down to find people.
Salvation has two sides. The death of Jesus deals with our sinful nature and our sinful deeds; the resurrection of Jesus gives us new life. The first is forgiveness, the second is rebirth. All of it is free. He does not take you in once you improve; you improve because He has already taken you in. The only thing you must do is put out your hand and receive.

禱告不是儀式，不是交易，也不是背誦。禱告就是跟父親說話。 所以不必文謅謅，不必跪:
Prayer is not a ritual, not a transaction, and not a recitation. Prayer is talking with your Father.
So there is no need for elegant phrasing, no need to kneel a long time, no need to compose your words first. You can talk with Him while driving, while washing dishes, before you fall asleep.
A simple frame: thanks first (what is there to be grateful for today), then confession (what do I know was wrong), then intercession (asking on behalf of others), and last of all your own needs. That order will slowly draw you out of yourself.

受洗不是入會儀式，是一場公開的葬禮與一場公開的生日。入水，表示舊人有己的生命與基:
Baptism is not an initiation ceremony. It is a public funeral and a public birthday. Going down into the water says that the old self-centred life has died with Christ; coming up out of the water says that the new selfless life is alive with Christ.
Baptism does not save anyone — faith saves. But baptism is the public declaration of that faith, and it is the Lord's own command. Believing quietly is a fine beginning; confessing openly is how a person grows.
What to prepare beforehand: a short testimony (life before Christ, the turning point, the change now), and a conversation with your family. What to remember afterwards: this is the starting line, not the finish. Now the one-to-one building begins.

建立每天固定的靈修節奏：讀經、禱告、記錄。生命的次序是先生命、再關係、後事工。: Build a steady daily rhythm: read, pray, record. The order of life is life first, then relationships, then ministry.
靈修不是一份要交的功課，是一場天天的約會。功課會讓人有罪惡感，約會讓人有期待感。:
Devotion is not homework to be handed in; it is a daily appointment. Homework makes a person feel guilty. An appointment makes a person look forward. The Lord Jesus said, “apart from me you can do nothing.” Notice He did not say “you will do rather worse.” He said “nothing” — a branch cut from the vine does not bear a little less fruit; it is dry within three days.
The practical rhythm is simple, three things: read, pray, record. Read a short passage a day, do not be greedy, and when you finish ask, “what does this show me about the kind of God He is?” Pray by speaking back to Him what you have just read, without religious language. Record one line, no more, of what God said to you today. A year later that one line a day will have become three hundred private sentences between you and God.
The order is life first, then relationships, then ministry. Many serve until they run dry, not because they did too much, but because they rushed out without first walking with the Lord. A pipe not joined to the source is empty however wide it is.

主耶穌說：「只等真理的聖靈來了，他要引導你們明白一切的真理。」聖靈不是一種感覺，:
The Lord Jesus said, “When he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth.” The Holy Spirit is not a feeling, nor a force. He is a personal God who lives within us. He guides, He reminds, He convicts, He comforts — and He can be grieved.
The Spirit lives in the heart, not in the head. So our habits must be adjusted: use the heart and rely on the Spirit, not the head and yourself. The heart brings gladness; the head brings worry. A person living out of his head is forever calculating — is this worth it, what will people think, what if I fail — and calculates himself into paralysis. A person living out of his heart asks: Lord, what would You have me do? And then does it.
How do you tell the Spirit's leading from your own notion? Four measures. First, does it agree with Scripture (the Spirit never leads anyone against the words He Himself wrote). Second, does it give the glory to Jesus (the Spirit does not exalt you). Third, is there peace in your heart or pressure (what God gives is peace within urgency; what Satan gives is urgency within panic). Fourth, is there confirmation from spiritual companions (in weighty matters, let godly people around you seek together with you).
The outcomes of a whole life flow from the heart. So the first thing to do each day is open your heart and say: Holy Spirit, please lead me today.
回想最近一次你「心裡有一個聲音」但你沒有理它。安靜下來問聖靈：那是祢嗎？如果是，: Recall the last time there was a voice in your heart that you ignored. Be still and ask the Spirit: was that You? If it was, do You still want me to do it?

耶穌是我的榜樣。焦點在耶穌，不在自己、不在別人、不在環境。: Jesus is my Role Model. The focus is on Jesus — not on myself, not on others, not on circumstances.
「你們當以基督耶穌的心為心。」保羅接著描寫的，是一條向下的路：祂本有神的形像，卻:
“Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus.” What Paul describes next is a downward road: though He was in the form of God, He emptied Himself, took the form of a servant, and became obedient to the point of death. That is the pattern of Jesus — not climbing up but going down; not seizing power but laying it down.
The most practical exercise in taking Jesus as our model is changing the focus. The rise and fall of our emotions in a day comes mostly from three wrong focal points: looking at self (am I performing well, am I losing face), looking at others (why did he say that about me), and looking at circumstances (why has something gone wrong again). Wherever the focus is, the emotions are. The focus is on Jesus — not on self, not on others, not on circumstances. Jesus is the focus of everything.
Learning Jesus is not imitating His actions; it is letting His life be lived out in me. You do not have to grit your teeth to love the person who is hard to love. What you must do is step aside and let the One who lives within you love him. This is why the next lesson is about selflessness: without it, following Christ becomes a tiring performance.

陪伴者提示：不要把這課講成道德要求。重點在「換焦點」，不在「更努力」。他若開始說: For companions: do not turn this lesson into a moral demand. The point is changing the focus, not trying harder. If he begins to say “I cannot do it,” that is good news — he is nearly ready for Lesson 5.
舊人有己的生命，變成新人無己的生命。這是一次成就、一生經歷的功課。: The old self-centred life becomes the new selfless life. This is accomplished once and experienced for a lifetime.
「就要脫去你們從前行為上的舊人……又要將你們的心志改換一新，並且穿上新人。」脫、:
“Put away the old man… be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man.” Put away, renew, put on — three actions showing that salvation is not a change of clothes but a change of person.
The old man has one defining word: self. Self at the centre of everything, self insisting on being master and king, self wanting to take God's place. This is not the problem of a few bad people; it is the common root disease of the whole race. Adam and Eve did not eat from the tree of knowledge out of appetite. They wanted to “be like God, knowing good and evil” — to be the one who defines right and wrong. So the root of sin is not conduct but self; the root of the problem is not other people but pride.
The new man also has one defining word: without. Selflessness — letting Jesus live within. This new life was given to you the moment Jesus rose; it is an accomplished fact, not a status to be earned by effort.
But there is a tension here. In standing, you are already the new man; in experience, the habits of the old man still leap out. That is why Paul says to put it away “daily.” This does not question your salvation; it describes your growth. Accomplished once, experienced for a lifetime — you are not striving for a new life, you are learning to live by the new life you already have.
求聖靈指出一個你最熟悉的「舊人反應」——那個一被踩到就自動跳出來的反應。不要辯解: Ask the Holy Spirit to point out the old-man reaction you know best — the one that leaps out automatically the moment someone treads on you. Do not defend it. Just see it.

當舊人跳出來時，不要自責，只說：「這是舊人，不是我了。主，求祢活出來。」: When the old man leaps out, do not condemn yourself. Simply say, “that is the old man; it is no longer me. Lord, live Your life out in me.”

陪伴者提示：這一課最容易變成自我控訴。要一再強調：看見舊人不是失敗的證據，是聖靈: For companions: this lesson turns into self-accusation more easily than any other. Say it again and again — seeing the old man is not evidence of failure but evidence that the Spirit is at work. A blind man cannot see his own dirt.
無己不是沒有，乃是進入無限、活出無限。無己讓耶穌在裡面活。: Selflessness is not having nothing; it is entering the infinite and living the infinite. Selflessness lets Jesus live within.
「我已經與基督同釘十字架，現在活著的不再是我，乃是基督在我裡面活著。」這節經文是:
“I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I that live, but Christ lives in me.” This verse is the heart of the whole discipleship course. Paul did not say “I try hard to imitate Christ.” He said “no longer I.”
Many people hear the word selflessness and take fright: does that mean I will be gone? Quite the opposite. Selflessness is not having nothing; it is entering the infinite and living the infinite. A drop of water standing alone dries up in the sun. A drop of water returned to the sea has all the vastness of the sea. Selflessness does not abolish you; it exchanges that small, cramped self for the boundless life of Christ.
Selflessness has five effects, worth committing to memory. Only the selfless can let Jesus reign. Only the selfless can be led by the Spirit. Only the selfless can be one. Only the selfless can overcome. Only the selfless can build the system that belongs to God. Turn it round and you find that everything we get stuck on — broken relationships, rivalry in ministry, powerless prayer — traces back to the same cause: self is still on the throne.
Denying self is an action; selflessness is a state. Denying self is taking up your own cross for Jesus and for others and not for yourself. Selflessness is what you discover after carrying that cross long enough: the one living inside really is no longer you.

陪伴者提示：不要用「你要無己」來壓人，那反而是律法。要幫他看見無己的甘甜——被基: For companions: do not press people with “you must be selfless” — that only turns into law. Help him taste how sweet selflessness is: to be so loved by Christ that you no longer need to prove yourself. What a release that is.
驕傲是離開本位抓住權力；謙卑是放下權力回到本位。讓人作人，讓神作神。: Pride leaves its place and seizes power; humility lays power down and returns to its place. Let man be man, and let God be God.
「神阻擋驕傲的人，賜恩給謙卑的人。」這節經文把屬靈爭戰的勝負講得非常直白：一邊是:
“God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.” This verse states the outcome of spiritual warfare with startling bluntness: on one side God Himself resists, on the other God freely gives. The same God, two utterly opposite postures, and the only difference is humility or pride.
What is pride? Pride leaves its place and seizes power — leaving the place of a man, seizing the authority of God, wanting to take God's place. So pride is not always a raised chin. A person who is anxious every day, who must control everything, who cannot let go, is also a kind of proud man: he is playing God.
What is humility? Humility lays power down and returns to its place — back to the place of a man, laying down the authority of God. In one line: let man be man, and let God be God.
Between people this principle produces a striking effect. Pride provokes pride; pride opposes pride; both are wounded. Humility draws out humility; humility meets humility; both win. So in a conflict the one who humbles himself first is not the loser — he is the one who unlocks the deadlock. Humility is the key to revival. Whether it is a family or a church, revival always begins when somebody is willing to bow first.
求聖靈照出：我的驕傲通常穿著什麼衣服？是強勢、是完美主義、是自卑不肯求助，還是什: Ask the Spirit to show you what clothes your pride usually wears. Is it forcefulness, perfectionism, a low self-worth that will not ask for help, or an anxiety that must manage everything?
我要放下神的權力，回到人的本位。讓人作人，讓神作神。: I will lay down the authority of God and return to the place of a man. Let man be man, and let God be God.
這週向一個人道歉——不是「如果我有錯」，是具體說出你錯在哪裡。: Apologise to one person this week — not “if I was wrong,” but naming exactly where you were wrong.
每天作一次「放手禱告」：把一件你一直想掌控的事交給神，說：「這件事祢作神，我作人: Pray a letting-go prayer each day: hand God one thing you keep trying to control, and say, “in this matter You be God and I will be man.”

陪伴者提示：這一課要陪伴者先示範。你在他面前承認過自己的失敗嗎？你若不先低頭，他: For companions: in this lesson the companion must go first. Have you ever admitted your own failure in front of him? If you will not bow first, he will never learn to bow.
不饒恕是把自己關在牢裡，卻等別人受苦。饒恕是先放自己出來。: Unforgiveness locks you in a cell and waits for the other person to suffer. Forgiveness lets yourself out first.
「並要以恩慈相待，存憐憫的心，彼此饒恕，正如神在基督裡饒恕了你們一樣。」饒恕的標:
“Be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.” The standard of forgiveness is not whether the other person deserves it, but “just as God forgave you.”
The great absurdity of unforgiveness is this: we lock ourselves in a cell and wait for the other person to suffer. You chew the matter over and over, and it is your own stomach that aches; he may have forgotten long ago. Forgiveness does not say the matter was nothing, nor that he was not wrong, nor that you must return at once to the old closeness. Forgiveness is a decision: I will no longer collect this debt with my own hands. I hand the account over to God.
Distinguish two things clearly. Forgiveness is one-sided; you can decide it yourself. Reconciliation is two-sided; it needs the other person's repentance and time. You may forgive someone who has never apologised, but you need not force yourself back into intimacy with someone who is still hurting you. Forgiveness releases you; reconciliation repairs the relationship.
Forgiveness is also seldom finished in one act. The deeper the wound, the more times you may have to hand the same matter over before God. Each time you hand it over, the binding loosens a little. That is not failure; that is the process of healing.
問聖靈：我心裡還關著誰？不必勉強自己有感覺，只要誠實地把那個名字說出來。: Ask the Spirit: whom am I still holding in my cell? Do not force a feeling. Just say the name honestly.
我選擇把討債的權利交還給神。我要先走出這座牢。: I choose to hand the right of collection back to God. I will walk out of this cell first.

陪伴者提示：不要催逼他饒恕，尤其是深度創傷。你的角色是陪他把傷口帶到主面前，不是: For companions: do not press him to forgive, especially with deep trauma. Your role is to carry the wound to the Lord with him, not to set his pace for him. Where needed, suggest professional help.
對每一個跟我有關係的人（2），操練無己（0），結出聖靈九個果子（9）。: Towards every person I am related to (the 2), practise selflessness (the 0), and bear the nine fruits of the Spirit (the 9).
920 是把靈修落在一個具體的人身上的操練。「9」是聖靈的九個果子：仁愛、喜樂、:
920 is the practice that lands your devotional life on one specific person. The 9 is the ninefold fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. The 2 is every person you are related to — your spouse, your child, your colleague, the neighbour who gives you a headache. Each of them is one of your 2s. The 0 is selflessness.
Notice that Paul writes “fruit” and not “fruits” — the original is singular. The nine are not nine skills to choose among; they are nine faces of one life. You cannot say, “I am better at joy, so I will skip patience.” They are a single cluster of grapes, growing together.
More importantly: fruit is borne, not wrung out. If you squeeze gentleness out of yourself, you will last three days and then snap, and snap harder than usual. The order is 0 first, then 9: be selfless, let Jesus live within, and the fruit grows from inside.
So the daily practice is very concrete: today, towards [this person], practise [this fruit]. Not an abstract “I want to be loving,” but “at lunch today, towards my mother, patience — when she asks a third time, I will not sigh.” Here is the truest groundwork for evangelism: people must first see the life of Christ before they can take in the teaching of Christ.
求聖靈指定一個人和一個果子。通常祂指的那一個，正是你最不想面對的那一個。: Ask the Spirit to name one person and one fruit. Usually the one He names is exactly the one you least want to face.
我不要擰出果子，我要無己，讓基督在我裡面結出果子。: I will not wring out fruit. I will be selfless and let Christ bear the fruit within me.

陪伴者提示：這是全課程最容易落地、也最容易放棄的一課。頭兩週每天傳一句提醒給他，: For companions: this is the easiest lesson in the course to put into practice and the easiest to abandon. For the first two weeks send him a one-line reminder every day. Once the habit is built, it runs by itself.
2 是屬靈同伴，3 是屬靈父母與兒女，5 是五重職份的團隊。體系從關係長出來。: The 2 is a spiritual companion, the 3 is spiritual parents and children, the 5 is a fivefold-ministry team. The system grows out of relationships.
「有兩人便能抵擋一人。三股合成的繩子不容易折斷。」屬靈生命不是單打獨鬥的競技，是:
“Two shall withstand him, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” Spiritual life is not a solo contest; it is the work of weaving a rope. 235 is the three strands of that rope.
The 2 is a spiritual companion: a peer, a level relationship of mutual support and mutual accountability. A companion is not there to correct you; he is there so that you need not pretend. Once one person knows your true condition, hypocrisy becomes very hard.
The 3 is spiritual parents and spiritual children: a relationship of handing down. A spiritual parent is not a spiritual superior. A parent's goal is that one day the child will no longer need him; a superior's goal is that more people will listen to him. That is the key distinction.
The 5 is spiritual comrades: a fivefold-ministry team — apostle, prophet, evangelist, pastor and teacher. Each has different gifts, and only in partnership can the saints be equipped, each doing his part, building up the body of Christ.
All three relationships require the same ticket of entry: selflessness. A self-centred person cannot build a system, because he is always weighing who matters more. Only the selfless can be one; only the selfless can build the system that belongs to God. Which strand are you missing today? That is most likely the strand the Lord is asking you to build.
問聖靈：我的2是誰？我的3在哪裡？我在哪一個5的團隊裡？哪一股是空的？: Ask the Spirit: who is my 2? Where is my 3? Which 5 team am I part of? Which strand is empty?
我不再單打獨鬥。我要主動去建立那條三股的繩子。: I will no longer fight alone. I will take the initiative to build that threefold cord.

問責五題：這週你與主如何？你有沒有隱藏的罪？你為誰禱告了？你關心了誰？你需要什麼: Five accountability questions: how have you been with the Lord this week? Is there hidden sin? Whom have you prayed for? Whom have you cared for? What help do you need?
為你的屬靈父母寫一段感謝的話，傳給他。: Write a paragraph of thanks to your spiritual parent and send it to him.
陪伴者提示：這一課要具體到名字。不要讓他停在「我知道要有同伴」，要在課堂上就打開: For companions: this lesson must get down to names. Do not let him stop at “I know I need a companion.” Open the contact list during the session and fix the first meeting time then and there.
人比事重要，關係比東西重要。不要為了事而傷害人，不要為了東西破壞關係。: People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. Do not wound a person for the sake of a task, or ruin a relationship for the sake of a thing.
「你們要先求他的國和他的義，這些東西都要加給你們了。」金錢、時間、工作，本身都不:
“Seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.” Money, time and work are not the enemy in themselves. Misplacement is. Reverse the order and a good thing becomes an idol.
This lesson asks you to remember two sentences: people matter more than tasks, relationships matter more than things. Therefore: do not wound a person for the sake of a task, and do not ruin a relationship for the sake of a thing. How many families never speak again over an inheritance; how many co-workers never serve together again over one argument about procedure. The task got done and the people scattered — that is a losing trade.
Money: how you use money shows who reigns in your heart. Giving does not mean God is short of funds; it means I make one concrete act of declaration — all of this was Yours to begin with.
Time: time management is really the ordering of values. When you say “I have no time,” the truth is usually “this is not far enough up my list.” Being honest about it actually makes it easier to change.
Work: work is the venue of service, not its rival. Your honesty in the workplace, your diligence, your refusal to take advantage — these are the most powerful witness. A colleague hearing thirty minutes of gospel from you is worth less than watching you keep three years of honest books.
求聖靈照出：我最近一次為了事而傷害人，是什麼時候？為了東西而讓關係變冷，又是哪一: Ask the Spirit to show you: when did I last wound a person for the sake of a task? And over which thing did a relationship grow cold?
人比事重要，關係比東西重要。我要先求神的國，其餘的交給祂加給我。: People matter more than tasks, relationships more than things. I will seek God's Kingdom first and leave the rest for Him to add.
檢視上個月的支出，問一句：這些錢說出我心裡誰在作王？: Review last month's spending and ask: what do these figures say about who reigns in my heart?

陪伴者提示：談錢容易讓人防衛。先分享你自己的掙扎與失敗，再問他。不要查帳，要同行: For companions: talk of money puts people on the defensive. Share your own struggles and failures first, then ask him. Do not audit — accompany.
服侍之路：靈、悟、命、侍、神。讓耶穌作王，讓耶穌得著一切的榮耀。: The path of service: Spirit, understanding, life, serving, God. Let Jesus reign, and let Jesus receive all the glory.
「各人要照所得的恩賜彼此服事，作神百般恩賜的好管家。」恩賜是託付，不是勳章。管家:
“As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God.” A gift is a trust, not a medal. Being a steward means the goods are not mine; I am only managing them for the Master.
The path of service has five words, which are both an order and a foundation. Spirit — the Holy Spirit is my Guide, so seek His leading and prompting first. Understanding — The Bible is my Standard, so grasp and obey the truth of Scripture. Life — Jesus is my Role Model, so cultivate and live out the life of Jesus. Serving — let Jesus reign, and serve by His authority and power. God — let Jesus receive all the glory.
Most weariness in service begins straight at the fourth word: skipping Spirit, understanding and life, and going directly to doing. That is doing God's work with your own strength, and it wounds you for as long as you keep it up.
Here is a simple test of gifting: when the work is done, do people's eyes land on you or on Jesus? If all they remember is how capable you are, that is not success in service but danger in it. Everything is what God has accomplished in Jesus; it is all grace. Give thanks in everything, and give the glory to Jesus.
問聖靈：我目前的服事，是從靈開始的，還是從侍開始的？我在服事中偷偷享受的，是主的: Ask the Spirit: does my present service begin at Spirit or at serving? And what am I secretly enjoying in it — the Lord's pleasure, or people's praise?
我是管家不是主人。我要靠聖靈服事，把一切榮耀歸給耶穌。: I am the steward, not the owner. I will serve by the Spirit and give all the glory to Jesus.

陪伴者提示：留意他是不是在用服事換取價值感。要幫他分清楚：他被愛，不是因為他有用: For companions: watch whether he is trading service for a sense of worth. Help him separate the two — he is loved, not because he is useful. If that distinction is left unaddressed, service will crush him sooner or later.
結業的標準不是上完了，是教過別人了。保羅、提摩太、忠心的人、別人——四代才叫體系: Completion is not “I finished it” but “I have taught someone else.” Paul, Timothy, faithful men, others — four generations is what makes a system.
「你在許多見證人面前聽見我所教訓的，也要交託那忠心能教導別人的人。」這一節經文裡:
“The things you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.” There are four generations in this one verse: Paul, Timothy, faithful men, others. Only after four generations can you call it a system.
This is the end of the whole discipleship course, and also a new beginning. We often get only as far as the second generation — we lead someone to Christ and then stop. The result is growth by addition, not reproduction by multiplication. A hundred believers each leading one person makes two hundred; but if every person led also learns to lead, four generations on you have a forest.
So completion is not “I finished it” but “I have taught someone else.” That single rule will change a church's constitution from the ground up, because it turns every person sitting and listening into a person standing and leading.
You may say: I am not good enough yet. A spiritual parent is not a perfect person; he is a person one step further along the road. You need not be a scholar. If you are one mile ahead of him, you have something to hand him. And when you teach another, you yourself will learn the most.

「我們既是這樣愛你們，不但願意將神的福音給你們，連自己的性命也願意給你們。」保羅:
“We were well pleased to impart to you not only the Good News of God, but also our own souls.” Paul names two things: the gospel, and himself. To give the gospel without giving yourself is to hand out a leaflet. To give yourself as well is to be a spiritual parent.
The first principle of walking with someone: be a friend first, do not rush to preach. Many evangelistic efforts fail right here — the subject is raised too soon, and the other person instantly feels he is a target rather than a friend. People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. At this stage your only task is to convince him: you really do care about me, you are not after my conversion.
The heart of walking with someone is not technique — it is not leaving. You need not be eloquent, you need not know theology. You need only actually turn up when things are hard for him. What most people remember all their lives is not who preached them a fine sermon, but who was still there on the night they were at their worst.
Walking with someone also needs boundaries. You are a parent, not a saviour. You can walk beside him; you cannot walk for him. You can pray for him; you cannot believe for him. Get that clear and you will last the distance.

「我不以福音為恥，這福音本是神的大能，要救一切相信的。」講福音的能力不在你的口才:
“I am not ashamed of the Good News, for it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes.” The power to share the gospel does not lie in your eloquence but in the gospel itself. Your responsibility is to make it clear, not to make anyone agree — persuading is the Holy Spirit's work.
Working the five acts in practice. Act One, a good beginning: cover it in a sentence, do not linger. Act Two, the fall into self: this is the hinge of the whole conversation, so slow down. Act Three, redemption at the cross: be concrete. Act Four, new life through resurrection: stress that this is available now, not an insurance policy for after death. Act Five, letting Jesus reign: give a clear invitation.
Why is Act Two the hinge? Because the moment we say “you are a sinner,” the other person's defences go up: I have not killed anyone. But if you say, “sin does not mean how much wrong you have done; it means I want to be my own master and king, and I do not want God running my life” — most people go quiet, because that is the story of their life.
Three techniques for the moment itself. First, tell your own story; do not only argue a case. Second, learn to pause — at the end of Act Two, stop and ask, “what do you think?” and let him speak. Third, invite him courageously. Many people never come to Christ simply because nobody ever formally asked them.

「有人問你們心中盼望的緣由，就要常作準備，以溫柔、敬畏的心回答各人。」注意經文的:
“Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear.” Note the two emphases: always be ready (so we must be equipped), and with humility and fear (so this is not about winning).
First principle: catch the feeling first, then handle the question. What hides under many questions is not an intellectual difficulty but a wounded experience. Take “why do good people suffer?” For one person it is a philosophical question; for another it is because his mother died last month. Same question, different answer. So the first move with every question is to ask back, “what made you think of that?”
Second principle: honestly admit what you do not know. Saying “I cannot answer that one; I will look into it and tell you next week” is far more persuasive than bluffing, and it gives you a reason to meet again.
Third principle: do not win the argument; win by love. Defeat him in debate and he will fall silent, but his heart will shut tighter. The purpose of an answer is not to win a debate but to open a door.
The forty questions in the answer library each have four layers: a one-sentence answer, a relevant passage, an everyday analogy, and a question to ask back. In practice, start with the fourth layer and use the first one last.

八大步驟的落實：資訊、啟示、信服、實踐、檢討、修正、反覆、繁殖。: Putting the eight steps to work: information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition, reproduction.
「我們傳揚他，是用諸般的智慧勸戒各人，教導各人，要把各人在基督裡完完全全地引到神:
“We proclaim him, admonishing every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man complete in Christ.” Paul's aim was not to finish the lesson but to present a person complete before God.
Discipleship is not a class; it is companionship. So the eight steps must not stop at the third. Information — tell him the truth. Revelation — pray quietly and ask the Spirit to let him see. Conviction — ask him “what does this mean for you?” and wait for it to travel from head to heart. Practice — give him a concrete seven-day action. Review — make the first item of next week's meeting a look back at last week's action. Correction — where he is stuck, adjust the method with him. Repetition — return to the same theme three months later. Reproduction — have him teach this lesson to someone else.
Most discipleship fails between step four and step five: the teaching is finished, but nobody walks with him through practice and review. So knowledge piles up and life does not move.
Three practicalities for leading discipleship. First, a fixed time — better short and regular than long and occasional. Second, do not speak for more than half of it; ask more questions and let him talk. Third, before each session ends, agree specifically on the next time and the next assignment.
Completion is not “we finished it” but “he has taught someone else.”

他不回訊息、他決志後消失了、他家人反對……忠心比成果重要。: He stops replying, he disappears after committing, his family objects… Faithfulness matters more than results.
「我們行善，不可喪志；若不灰心，到了時候就要收成。」保羅沒有說不會累，他說不要喪:
“Let's not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don't give up.” Paul did not say you will not get tired. He said do not lose heart. Tiredness is a matter of the body; losing heart is a matter of the soul.
The most common discouragements: he no longer replies to me; he vanished after making his commitment; his family objects fiercely; he believed but nothing changed; I have walked with him three years and he is just the same. Every one of them starts a person doubting himself.
A few sentences to hold on to. First, I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth — growth is not your responsibility, faithfulness is. Second, no response is not the same as no effect; while the seed is in the soil it cannot be seen. Third, your worth is not determined by results; if numbers determine your worth, sooner or later you will hurt people for the sake of a figure.
What to do in practice: tell your spiritual companion, do not carry it alone; write the discouragement down and bring it into prayer rather than letting it ferment inside; and keep a record of the signs that the Lord is at work — those very small changes are the food of your faith through a long wait.
One more thing to say honestly: sometimes the problem is not his, it is that we are in too much of a hurry. Stopping to ask a question is often more use than another push.

「不是你們揀選了我，是我揀選了你們，並且分派你們去結果子，叫你們的果子常存。」注:
“You didn't choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain.” Note the word remain — fruit that remains is fruit that will bear fruit again.
Reproduction is the final test of a spiritual parent. Real success is not how much he needs you but that he no longer needs you and has begun a list of his own. This runs against human nature: we like being needed. If you find you cannot bear to let go, face it honestly — that is usually not for his good; it is our own self still in place.
Four steps of releasing, worth memorising: I do, you watch; I do, you help; you do, I help; you do, I watch. Most people stall at the second step and will not move on, and end up ten years later still playing nursemaid.
Make opportunities on purpose. Take him along to care for someone and let him watch from the side. Next time let him speak and you fill in the gaps. The time after that, say nothing at all. On the way home, ask him first, “how do you think that went?” and then give feedback — two affirmations first, then one adjustment.
Finally, pray for his spiritual children. On the day you see your spiritual grandchild born, you will understand why Paul spoke of four generations. A system is not an organisation chart; it is one generation of real lives after another.
問聖靈：我現在陪伴的人裡，誰已經可以往前一步了？我卡在放手的哪一個階段？: Ask the Spirit: among those I am walking with, who is ready to take a step forward? And at which stage of letting go am I stuck?
真正的成功，是他不再需要我，並且有了他自己的名單。: Real success is that he no longer needs me and has a list of his own.
評估你的每一位屬靈兒女，現在各在哪一步：我作你看／我作你幫／你作我幫／你作我看。: Assess each of your spiritual children and where each one now stands: I do you watch / I do you help / you do I help / you do I watch.
挑一位，本週帶他一起去關心另一個人。: Choose one and take him along this week to care for someone else.
下一次讓他主導，你只在旁邊。回程給他兩個肯定、一個調整。: Next time let him lead while you stay at his side. On the way home give him two affirmations and one adjustment.
陪他寫下他自己的第一張名單。: Sit with him as he writes his own first list.
為你的屬靈孫子禱告——即使他還沒有出現。: Pray for your spiritual grandchild — even before he appears.
本課實作：畫出你的屬靈家譜樹，看見自己在第幾代，並寫下你希望三年後這棵樹長成什麼: In-class exercise: draw your spiritual family tree, see which generation you stand in, and write down what you hope the tree will look like three years from now.
在一切的起頭，有一位神。祂造了光、造了海、造了會開花的樹，最後祂造了人——不是隨:
At the very beginning there was God. He made light, He made the sea, He made trees that flower — and last of all He made man, not casually, but in His own image. He breathed the breath of life into man's nostrils, and man became a living soul.
In those days there was nothing between man and God. God walked in the garden and man could hear His footsteps. Man had nothing to prove and nothing to fight for, because he knew he was loved.
So the emptiness in you that keeps saying “something is missing” is not a fault in you. You were made for a God in the first place.
問題不是從殺人放火開始的。是從一個念頭開始的：「我可以自己決定什麼是對、什麼是錯:
The trouble did not begin with murder or arson. It began with a thought: “I can decide for myself what is right and what is wrong.” What the serpent said was, “you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
Man did not eat that fruit because he was hungry. He ate it because he wanted the seat. That is pride: leaving the place of a man, seizing the authority of God, wanting to take God's place.
This is the root of what the Bible calls sin, and we call it self — making myself the centre of everything, insisting on being master and king.
The moment self comes in, four cracks open at once: man is cut off from God, man is at odds with himself, people begin shifting blame and wounding one another, and man's world falls out of order.
So you need not begin by admitting you are a bad person. You need only ask one honest question: who has been reigning over my life?
神大可以放手不管，但祂沒有。祂做了一件我們無法想像的事——祂自己來了。 耶穌基督:
God could well have left us to it, but He did not. He did something beyond our imagining — He came Himself.
Jesus Christ, the Son of God, became a real man, walked in the dust, went hungry, grew tired, was misunderstood. In the end He was nailed to a cross. What He bore that day was not only the wrong we have done (our sinful deeds) but the nature inside us that insists on being its own master (our sinful nature).
It was an exchange: He took what we deserved, and we receive what He deserved. He did not haggle. He did it willingly.
So the cross is not a religious symbol. It is a receipt marked paid in full.
如果故事停在十字架，那只是一個好人的悲劇。但第三天，墳墓空了。 耶穌的復活成就了:
If the story stopped at the cross, it would be only the tragedy of a good man. But on the third day the tomb was empty.
The resurrection of Jesus accomplished a second thing: He does not merely forgive your past, He gives you a wholly new life. The old self-centred life was nailed to the cross; the new selfless life has been given.
This is the best news the gospel carries. You are not being told, “from now on try hard to be a good person.” You are being given a new life, so that Christ may live it out within you.
No longer I, but Christ. This is not you pushing harder; this is you changing masters.
現在只剩一件事：你願不願意讓祂進來，把生命的主權交給祂。 這不是簽一份合約，是打:
One thing remains: whether you are willing to let Him in and hand Him the rule of your life.
This is not signing a contract; it is opening a door. God will not force His way in. He knocks from outside and waits for you to open.
To believe means: I admit I have been reigning over my own life and I have not done it well; I believe Jesus died for me and rose for me; from today I invite Him in and let Him reign.
This step does not require you to improve first. It requires only that you are willing. And whoever is willing may take the water of life freely.
不用背，也不用講得好聽。跟著念，或用自己的話說都可以。神聽的是心。: Nothing to memorise, nothing to make sound impressive. Read it after me, or use your own words. What God listens to is the heart.
親愛的主耶穌： 我來到你面前。 我承認我這一生都是自己作主、自己作王，凡事以自己:
Dear Lord Jesus,
I come to You.
I admit that all my life I have been my own master and my own king, with myself at the centre of everything. I have not done it well, and I am tired.
I believe You died on the cross for me and bore my sin; I believe You rose from the dead on the third day to give me new life.
Now I open the door of my heart and ask You to come in.
I am willing for You to be the Lord of my life and to reign within me.
Forgive me, cleanse me, and live Your life in me.
From today I am no longer walking alone.
In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray. Amen.

適合等車、排隊、飯後閒聊的空檔。目標不是講完，是讓他想再聽。: For waiting at a bus stop, standing in a queue, chatting after a meal. The aim is not to finish, but to leave him wanting to hear more.

適合已經有信任基礎、他也開始問問題的階段。原則是：他講的時間要比你多。: For when trust is established and he has begun asking questions himself. The rule: he should talk more than you do.
我用三分鐘跟你講一件對我最重要的事，好不好？講完你當笑話聽也沒關係。: May I take three minutes to tell you the thing that matters most to me? If it sounds like a joke to you afterwards, that is fine.
聖經說，人本來是神照著自己的形像造的，人跟神原本是很近的。所以我們心裡總覺得少一: The Bible says man was made in God's own image, and that man and God were once very close. So the piece that always feels missing inside us is not actually a fault in us.
後來出問題了。問題不是從殺人放火開始，是從一個念頭開始的——「我要自己作主」。聖: Then something went wrong. It did not start with murder or arson; it started with a thought — “I will be my own master.” The Bible calls this the root of sin, and we call it self: making myself the centre of everything and wanting to take God's place.
你想想看，我們一生的煩惱，是不是大半都出在這裡？想控制、想贏、想被看見。: Think about it — is that not where most of our troubles come from? Wanting control, wanting to win, wanting to be noticed.
神的解決辦法不是給我們一本規矩。祂自己來了。耶穌被釘在十字架上，替我們承擔了這一: God's answer was not to hand us a rule book. He came Himself. Jesus was nailed to a cross and bore all of it in our place, and on the third day He rose, in order to give us a wholly new life.
所以信耶穌不是變得更會守規矩，是換一個生命，讓祂在我裡面作王。: So believing in Jesus is not getting better at keeping rules. It is exchanging one life for another, and letting Him reign within me.
祂現在就站在你心門外敲門，門把在你這邊。哪一天你願意開，隨時可以告訴我，我陪你。: He is standing at the door of your heart knocking right now, and the handle is on your side. Whenever you are willing to open it, tell me, and I will be with you.
【開場】我想跟你分享一個故事，這個故事有五幕。你隨時可以打斷我、隨時可以問。: [Opening] I would like to share a story with you. It has five acts. Stop me at any time, ask at any time.
【第一幕 美好的起初】聖經第一句話是「起初，神創造天地」。祂造了萬物，最後照著自: [Act One: A Good Beginning] The Bible's first line is “in the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.” He made all things, and last of all He made man in His own image. In those days there was nothing between man and God; man had nothing to prove, because he knew he was loved. So the emptiness in us that says “something is missing” is not a defect. It is the factory setting — we were made for a God in the first place.
【停一下】你有沒有過那種感覺？什麼都有了，還是覺得空？: [Pause] Have you ever felt that? You have everything, and still feel empty?
【第二幕 有己的墮落】問題怎麼開始的？蛇對人說：「你們便如神能知道善惡。」人吃那: [Act Two: The Fall Into Self] How did the trouble begin? The serpent said to man, “you will be like God, knowing good and evil.” Man did not eat that fruit because he was hungry, but because he wanted God's seat. That is pride — leaving the place of a man and seizing the authority of God. The Bible calls it sin; we call it self: making myself the centre of everything, insisting on being master and king. The moment self comes in, four cracks appear: man cut off from God, man at odds with himself, people wounding one another, and man's world out of order.
【停一下】你覺得，人最大的問題是行為不好，還是裡面那個「我要自己作主」？: [Pause] Which do you think is man's biggest problem — bad behaviour, or that thing inside that says “I will be my own master”?
【第三幕 十架的救贖】神沒有放手不管。祂自己來了。耶穌成為一個真實的人，最後被釘: [Act Three: Redemption at the Cross] God did not leave us to it. He came Himself. Jesus became a real man, and in the end was nailed to a cross. What He bore was not only the wrong we have done, but the nature inside us that insists on being master. It was an exchange: He took what we deserved, and we receive what He deserved.
【第四幕 復活的新生命】如果故事停在這裡，只是一個好人的悲劇。但第三天，墳墓空了: [Act Four: New Life Through Resurrection] If the story stopped here it would be only the tragedy of a good man. But on the third day the tomb was empty. The resurrection accomplished a second thing — He does not merely forgive your past, He gives you a wholly new life. The old self-centred life was nailed to the cross; the new selfless life was given. Paul said: it is no longer I that live, but Christ lives in me.
【停一下】如果不是靠你更努力，而是有一個新生命被賜下來，這對你有沒有吸引力？: [Pause] If this is not about you trying harder but about a new life being given to you, does that appeal to you at all?
【第五幕 讓耶穌作王】現在只剩一件事：你願不願意讓祂進來作王。祂不會硬闖，祂在門: [Act Five: Let Jesus be King] One thing remains: whether you are willing to let Him in to reign. He will not force His way; He knocks at the door. Believing is not improving first and then coming. If you are willing, you may come.
【誠實說明】我也要老實告訴你：信主不保證從此順利，有時候家人還會反對。但你會多一: [An honest word] I should tell you plainly: believing does not guarantee smooth sailing, and sometimes family will object. But you will gain a companion who never leaves, and your life really will begin to be different.
【邀請】所以我想問你一句話——你願意現在就接受祂嗎？: [Invitation] So let me ask you one question — would you be willing to receive Him now?
【先聽，不先講】今天我不急著講什麼，我想先聽你說。可以跟我說說，你這一路走來，最: [Listen first, speak later] I am in no hurry to say anything today; I would rather listen to you first. Would you tell me which stretch of the road has been hardest for you?
【接住他】（他說的時候不要急著給答案，也不要急著轉入信仰。真的聽完，並且回應他的: [Catch him] (While he speaks, do not rush to answer and do not rush to turn the conversation to faith. Really hear him out, and respond to what he is feeling.)

【第一幕】我後來才明白，人心裡那個填不滿的空，是有來歷的。聖經說人是照著神的形像: [Act One] Only later did I understand that the emptiness inside us has a history. The Bible says man was made in God's image — we were made for a God in the first place.
【第二幕】而我們的問題也有一個很準確的診斷。不是「你做了什麼壞事」，是「我要自己: [Act Two] And our problem has a very precise diagnosis. It is not “what wrong have you done” but “I will be my own master.” The Bible calls it sin, and this self cuts man off from God and from other people. I am the best example of it myself — (give a real instance of your own wanting control or wanting to win).
【第三幕】神的辦法不是要我改進，是祂親自來替我死。十字架上，祂處理的不只是我做過: [Act Three] God's answer was not to make me improve. He came in person to die in my place. At the cross He dealt not only with the wrong I had done, but with the old self that I am.
【第四幕】而祂復活了。這一點對我最關鍵——因為我試過靠自己變好，我做不到。祂復活: [Act Four] And He rose. That is the crucial point for me, because I had tried to get better on my own and I could not. He rose in order to give me His life, so that Christ might live in me.
【第五幕】所以現在祂站在你的門外敲門。祂不會闖進來，祂等你開。: [Act Five] So now He stands knocking at your door. He will not break in. He waits for you to open.

Some people may not understand you, and some habits will take time to change. But I can promise you two things: you will no longer be alone, and you will see with your own eyes that you are becoming different.
【明確邀請】我想正式地問你一次：你願意現在把生命的主權交給耶穌嗎？如果願意，我可: [A clear invitation] Let me ask you formally, once: would you be willing to hand the rule of your life over to Jesus now? If you are, I can lead you in a very simple prayer.
【若他說還沒準備好】完全沒關係，我等你。我會繼續為你禱告，我們照樣是朋友。: [If he says he is not ready] That is completely all right. I will wait for you. I will keep praying for you, and we are friends just the same.

罪得赦免，與神和好，不再需要靠表現換取被愛。: Sins forgiven, peace with God, and no more earning love by performance.
有一位永不離開的同在，最難的時候也不再一個人。: A presence that never leaves, so that even in the hardest hour you are not alone.

如果只剩一年，你會怎麼過？: If you had one year left, how would you spend it?

最近有沒有什麼事讓你睡不好？: Has anything been keeping you from sleeping well lately?

你對宗教的印象是什麼？好的壞的都可以說。: What impression do you have of religion? Good or bad, say either.

你有沒有被哪個宗教的人傷過？: Have you ever been hurt by someone from a religion?

我們因著信，就知道諸世界是藉神話造成的；這樣，所看見的，並不是從顯然之物造出來的: By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made out of things which are visible.
起初，神創造天地。: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
你們尋求我，若專心尋求我，就必尋見。: You shall seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
在世上，你們有苦難；但你們可以放心，我已經勝了世界。: In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.
神要擦去他們一切的眼淚；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭號、疼痛，因為以前的事都過去: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more, for the first things have passed away.
我們曉得萬事都互相效力，叫愛神的人得益處。: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God.
我的恩典夠你用的，因為我的能力是在人的軟弱上顯得完全。: My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.
天地要廢去，我的話卻不能廢去。: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
聖經都是神所默示的，於教訓、督責、使人歸正、教導人學義都是有益的。: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness.
這些事我既從起頭都詳細考察了，就定意要按著次序寫給你。: It seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order.
草必枯乾，花必凋殘，惟有我們神的話必永遠立定。: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.
耶和華，耶和華，是有憐憫有恩典的神，不輕易發怒，並有豐盛的慈愛和誠實。: Yahweh, Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.
耶穌說：我就是道路、真理、生命；若不藉著我，沒有人能到父那裡去。: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.”
審判全地的主豈不行公義嗎？: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
口渴的人也當來；願意的，都可以白白取生命的水喝。: He who is thirsty, let him come. He who desires, let him take the water of life freely.
立志為善由得我，只是行出來由不得我。: For desire is present with me, but I don't find it doing that which is good.
我是好牧人，好牧人為羊捨命。: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
你怎麼證明有神？: How can you prove there is a God?
神不是實驗室裡的一個物件，祂是萬有的源頭。我們證明祂，不是把祂放上天平，而是看見: God is not an object in a laboratory; He is the source of all things. We do not prove Him by putting Him on a scale, but by seeing the traces He has left: the order of the universe, the wonder of life, and the ruler of right and wrong inside the human heart.
你走進一間屋子，桌上茶還溫著，燈亮著，門是關上的。你不會說「這屋子從來沒有人」，: You walk into a house. The tea on the table is still warm, the lamp is on, the door is shut. You do not say “nobody has ever been here.” You say “someone was here a moment ago.” The universe is that house.
如果真的有一位神，你希望祂是怎樣的一位神？: If there really is a God, what kind of God would you hope He is?
科學回答「怎麼運作」，信仰回答「為什麼存在」。科學不能證明神，正如顯微鏡不能證明: Science answers how things work; faith answers why they exist. Science cannot prove God, just as a microscope cannot prove a mother's love. It is not that the love is absent; it is that the wrong instrument was used.
把一鍋湯拿去化驗，可以驗出鹽分、脂肪、蛋白質，卻驗不出「這是媽媽煮的」。驗不出來: Send a pot of soup to the laboratory and you can measure the salt, the fat and the protein, but you cannot measure “my mother made this.” Failing to measure it does not mean there is no mother.
你生命裡最重要的那些事——愛、意義、值不值得——有哪一件是靠科學證明才相信的？: Of the things that matter most in your life — love, meaning, whether something is worth it — which one did you believe only after science proved it?
宇宙是怎麼來的？: Where did the universe come from?
科學告訴我們宇宙有一個開始，那就表示它不是自有的。凡有開始的，必有使它開始的。基: Science tells us the universe had a beginning, which means it is not self-existent. Whatever has a beginning must have something that began it. The Christian faith says the One who began it is God.
一列火車，第一節車廂被第二節推動，第二節被第三節推動……推到最後你總得問：最前面: On a train, the first carriage is pushed by the second, the second by the third, and so on. Eventually you must ask: what set the front one moving? There has to be a mover that needs no pushing.
你覺得「一切都是偶然」和「一切都有心意」，哪一個比較需要信心？: Which do you think takes more faith — that everything is accidental, or that everything is intended?
感覺不到，不代表不存在，很多時候是因為我們忙到聽不見，或者心裡有一堵牆。神從來沒: Not feeling something does not mean it is not there. Often we are simply too busy to hear, or there is a wall inside. God has never left; we have shut Him outside the door.
收音機一直有訊號，是我們沒有調到那個頻道。頻道不對，不是電台沒播音。: The radio signal is always there; we have simply not tuned to the station. The wrong dial does not mean the station stopped broadcasting.
如果有一天你真的感覺到了，你願意怎麼回應祂？: If one day you really did sense Him, how would you want to respond?
如果有神，為何祂不現身？: If there is a God, why doesn't He show Himself?
祂現身過。兩千年前，祂成為一個嬰孩降生，走在人群中間，最後為我們死在十字架上。神: He has shown Himself. Two thousand years ago He was born a child, walked among crowds, and finally died for us on a cross. God has not hidden Himself away; He walked in.
如果太陽為了讓螞蟻看清楚它，直接靠過來，螞蟻不會看見太陽，只會被燒掉。所以太陽選: If the sun came close so that an ant could see it clearly, the ant would not see the sun — it would simply burn. So the sun chose instead to become a warm ray of light. Jesus is that light.
如果神真的來過，而且是以受苦的方式來的，這跟你原本想像的神有什麼不一樣？: If God really did come, and came by way of suffering, how is that different from the God you had imagined?
苦難不是神的懲罰清單，是這個已經破碎的世界的共同處境。福音真正的答案不是解釋苦難: Suffering is not God's list of punishments; it is the shared condition of a world already broken. The gospel's real answer is not an explanation of suffering, but that God walked into it Himself and bore it alongside us.
孩子半夜發燒，父母給的不是一篇「為什麼會發燒」的論文，是整夜守在床邊的那隻手。神: When a child runs a fever at midnight, what the parents give is not an essay on the causes of fever but a hand that stays by the bed all night. What God gives us is that hand.
你現在最想有人陪你走過的，是哪一段？: Right now, which stretch of the road would you most like someone to walk with you through?
神給了人真實的自由，而自由必然帶著被濫用的可能。祂沒有選擇做一個把人變成木偶的神: God gave man real freedom, and freedom necessarily carries the possibility of abuse. He did not choose to be a God who turns people into puppets. He chose to be present with people in disaster, and to make all things new at the last.
父母若把孩子鎖在家裡一輩子，孩子確實不會受傷，但那也不叫人生了。愛必須冒險，因為: If parents locked a child indoors for life, the child would indeed never be hurt — but that would not be a life either. Love must take risks, because love can only happen where there is freedom.
你希望神現在就把所有惡都除掉嗎？那你我會不會也在那份名單上？: Would you want God to remove all evil right now? And if He did, might you and I be on that list too?
我的家人早逝，神在哪裡？: My family member died young. Where was God?
祂就在你哭的地方。聖經裡耶穌站在朋友的墳墓前，明明知道下一刻要叫他復活，仍然先哭: He was in the place where you wept. In the Bible, Jesus stood before His friend's tomb knowing He was about to raise him — and He wept first anyway. God does not stand at a distance watching you hurt. He is the One who hurts alongside you.
最深的安慰從來不是一句「別難過了」，是有人坐下來，什麼也不說，陪你到天亮。: The deepest comfort has never been “don't be sad.” It is someone sitting down, saying nothing, and staying with you until morning.
願意跟我說說他是個怎樣的人嗎？我想認識他。: Would you tell me what he was like? I would like to know him.
神既全能又全善，為何有惡？: If God is all-powerful and all-good, why is there evil?
惡不是神造的一樣東西，惡是「善的缺席」，是受造者離開本位、要自己作主的結果。神容: Evil is not a thing God made. Evil is the absence of good — the result of a creature leaving his proper place and insisting on being his own master. God permits evil to exist for a time because what He wants is not robots but children who are willing to love Him.
黑暗不是一種物質，是沒有光。冷不是一種能量，是沒有熱。惡也一樣——它是人離開神以: Darkness is not a substance; it is the absence of light. Cold is not an energy; it is the absence of heat. Evil is the same — it is the hollow left behind when man walked away from God.
你心裡真正在意的，是「惡為什麼存在」這個問題，還是某一件具體發生在你身上的事？: What is really weighing on you — the question of why evil exists, or one particular thing that happened to you?
我信了就不會受苦嗎？: If I believe, will I stop suffering?
不會。信耶穌不是買保險，是換一個生命。苦難仍會來，但你不再是一個人面對，而且苦難: No. Believing in Jesus is not buying insurance; it is exchanging one life for another. Suffering will still come, but you will no longer face it alone, and in His hands suffering becomes something that builds you.
同樣一場大雨，沒傘的人是災難，有傘的人也一樣淋到風、聽到雷，但他能走完那條路。信: In the same downpour, a man without an umbrella meets disaster. A man with one still feels the wind and hears the thunder, but he can finish the road. Faith does not cancel the rain; it gives you the strength to keep walking.
如果苦難不會消失，但你有一位永遠不離開的同伴，這樣的信仰對你有意義嗎？: If suffering will not disappear, but you had a companion who never leaves, would that kind of faith mean anything to you?
為何禱告沒有得到答應？: Why hasn't my prayer been answered?
神對禱告的回答有三種：好、等一等、我有更好的。沒有一種是「不理你」。有時候祂不改: God's answers to prayer come in three forms: yes, wait, and I have something better. Not one of them is being ignored. Sometimes He does not change the circumstances because He means to change us first.
孩子要一把水果刀，爸爸沒有給。不是爸爸不愛他，是爸爸看得比較遠。: A child asks for a fruit knife and his father does not give it. It is not that the father does not love him; the father simply sees further.
你最近最想求神成就的那件事，可以跟我說嗎？我想陪你一起求。: What is the thing you most want God to do for you at the moment? Tell me, and I would like to ask for it with you.
聖經是古代抄本數量最多、年代最早的文獻。死海古卷發現的以賽亞書抄本，比原先所有的: The Bible has more ancient manuscripts, and earlier ones, than any other document from antiquity. The scroll of Isaiah found among the Dead Sea Scrolls is a thousand years older than any manuscript we previously had, and its contents are almost identical. It stands up to examination.
一份文件如果只有一份，改了沒人知道。但如果同一份文件散在幾千個地方、幾百種語言、: If a document exists in one copy, it can be altered and nobody will know. But if the same document is spread over thousands of places, hundreds of languages and several centuries, any alteration is caught immediately by comparison. That is the Bible's situation.
如果聖經真的可信，你最想先看哪一卷？我可以陪你讀。: If the Bible really is reliable, which book would you want to read first? I could read it with you.
聖經裡的矛盾怎麼解釋？: How do you explain the contradictions in the Bible?
多數所謂的矛盾，來自角度不同或文體不同，就像四個人描述同一場車禍。真正難解的地方: Most so-called contradictions come from different vantage points or different literary forms, like four people describing the same traffic accident. Genuinely difficult passages do exist, but not one of them shakes the core of the gospel.
四個證人若說得一字不差，法官反而要懷疑他們串供。細節有差異，主軸卻一致，這才是真: If four witnesses gave word-for-word identical accounts, the judge would suspect collusion. Differing in detail while agreeing on the main line — that is what real testimony looks like.
你讀到哪一段覺得對不起來？我們一起查查看，我也想知道。: Which passage did you find did not add up? Let us look into it together; I would like to know too.
聖經只是古人的神話嗎？: Isn't the Bible just ancient mythology?
神話沒有地名、沒有年代、沒有可查證的人物。聖經卻滿是可考的君王、城市、碑文與年份: Myths have no place names, no dates, no verifiable people. The Bible is full of kings, cities, inscriptions and years that can be checked. It submits itself to historical examination.
神話開頭是「很久很久以前，在一個遙遠的國度」；路加福音開頭是「該撒亞古士督在位的: A myth opens with “long, long ago, in a faraway kingdom.” Luke opens with “in the days of Caesar Augustus, when Quirinius was governor of Syria.” That is how news is written, not fairy tales.
如果它真的是歷史，而不是故事，這對你會有差別嗎？: If it really is history rather than story, would that make a difference to you?
為什麼有那麼多版本？: Why are there so many versions?
版本多是因為翻譯多、語言在變，不是因為內容被改。就像同一本書有不同譯者，原文卻只: There are many versions because there are many translations and because languages change, not because the contents were altered. One book may have several translators, but there is only one original.
同一首歌，有人用鋼琴彈，有人用吉他唱，曲子沒有變。譯本是樂器，原文是曲譜。: The same song may be played on a piano or sung with a guitar; the song itself has not changed. Translations are the instruments; the original is the score.
你想從哪一本開始讀？我推薦和合本或現代中文譯本，看你讀哪個順。: Which edition would you like to start with? I would suggest whichever reads more easily for you.
舊約的神為何那麼嚴厲？: Why is the God of the Old Testament so severe?
舊約的神和新約的神是同一位。祂的嚴厲從來針對的是壓迫、殘忍與獻嬰的邪惡，而祂的耐: The God of the Old Testament and the God of the New are one and the same. His severity was always aimed at oppression, cruelty and the evil of child sacrifice, and His patience was such that He waited centuries before acting. And in the end that same God chose to let His own Son bear all the judgement.
一個對癌症不動刀的醫生，不叫慈愛，叫失職。神的嚴厲，是祂對邪惡認真；祂的十字架，: A doctor who will not operate on cancer is not kind; he is negligent. God's severity is Him taking evil seriously; God's cross is Him taking us seriously.
你比較介意一位對惡不聞不問的神，還是一位會處理惡的神？: Which would trouble you more — a God who ignores evil, or a God who deals with it?
條條大路通羅馬，為何只有基督教？: All roads lead to Rome — so why only Christianity?
問題不在哪條路，在於「誰走得動」。所有宗教都在教人怎麼爬上去見神，只有福音說：神: The question is not which road, but who is able to walk it. Every religion teaches people how to climb up to God; only the gospel says God came down to find people. These are not competitors of the same kind; they run in opposite directions.
掉進深井的人，井上遞下來的繩子只有一條——不是因為繩子霸道，是因為別的都是畫在牆: For a man fallen down a deep well, only one rope is lowered — not because the rope is domineering, but because the others are painted on the wall.
你會怎麼描述你心中那位神？我很想知道你是怎麼想的。: How would you describe the God in your own mind? I would really like to know what you think.
沒聽過福音的人怎麼辦？: What about people who have never heard the gospel?
神是公義的，祂必按各人所領受的光審判，我們可以把這一題安心交給祂。但有一件事我很: God is just, and He will judge each person by the light that person received; we can leave that question with Him without anxiety. But of one thing I am certain: you have now heard. So this question has actually become a question about you.
船難時救生艇來了，你不會先問「還沒被找到的人怎麼辦」，你會先上船，然後幫忙划回去: When the lifeboat arrives at a shipwreck, you do not first ask what will happen to those not yet found. You get in, and then you help row back to look for them.
既然你已經聽見了，你打算怎麼回應？: Now that you have heard, how do you intend to respond?
真理本來就有排他性，2＋2＝4 就排斥了 5，這不叫傲慢，叫誠實。但基督信仰在「: Truth is exclusive by nature. Two plus two making four excludes five, and that is not arrogance but honesty. Yet on the question of who may come, the Christian faith is the most inclusive in the world — whoever you are and whatever you have done, you may come.

有智慧的，必能得人。: He who is wise wins souls.
但聖靈降臨在你們身上，你們就必得著能力，並要在……直到地極，作我的見證。: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be witnesses to me… to the uttermost parts of the earth.
你們往普天下去，傳福音給萬民聽。: Go into all the world and preach the Good News to the whole creation.
你們若有彼此相愛的心，眾人因此就認出你們是我的門徒了。: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.

不但願意將神的福音給你們，連自己的性命也願意給你們。: We were well pleased to impart to you not only the Good News of God, but also our own souls.
若不是耶和華建造房屋，建造的人就枉然勞力。: Unless Yahweh builds the house, they who build it labour in vain.

我也要賜給你們一個新心，將新靈放在你們裡面。: I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you.
主……不願有一人沉淪，乃願人人都悔改。: The Lord is… not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
他願意跟你說心裡的事: He is willing to tell you what is on his mind
許多福音行動失敗在這裡：太快切入主題，對方覺得自己是「目標」不是「朋友」。人比事: Many evangelistic efforts fail right here: the subject is raised too soon and the other person feels like a target rather than a friend. People matter more than tasks, relationships more than things. Your only task at this stage is to convince him: you really do care about me, you are not after my conversion.
記住並主動關心他的重要日子與難處: Remember his important dates and difficulties, and ask after them without being prompted
在他有需要時真的出現、真的幫忙: Actually turn up and actually help when he is in need
為他每日禱告，一天不斷: Pray for him daily, without missing a day
傳一則問候，不提任何信仰的事: Send one message just to say hello, with nothing about faith in it
記下他最近的一個難處，這週為這件事禱告: Note one difficulty he has at the moment, and pray for it this week
找一件小事實際幫他一次: Find one small thing and actually help him with it
問他一個關於生活的開放問題（見破冰問題）: Ask him one open question about his life (see the ice-breaker questions)
他主動問起信仰的事: He asks about faith of his own accord
撒種不是講道理，是分享「發生在我身上的事」。最有力量的不是「聖經說」，是「上個月: Sowing is not arguing a case; it is sharing what happened to me. The most powerful opening is not “the Bible says” but “something happened to me last month.” The aim is to move faith from a forbidden topic to an ordinary one.
分享個人的三分鐘見證（不談教義，只談改變）: Share your personal three-minute testimony (no doctrine, only what changed)
在合適時機邀請他一起吃飯、聽詩歌、看短片: At a suitable moment, invite him to share a meal, hear some music, or watch a short film
分享一段適合他處境的金句: Share a verse that fits the situation he is in
邀請他參加低門檻的活動（不是主日崇拜）: Invite him to something easy to walk into (not the Sunday service)
分享你見證裡的一小段，不用講完: Share one small part of your testimony; you need not finish it
傳一張適合他現在處境的金句給他: Send him a verse that fits where he is right now
邀他吃一頓飯，不談信仰也沒關係: Invite him for a meal; it is fine if faith never comes up
跟他說一句：我最近有為你禱告: Tell him one thing: I have been praying for you lately
他願意讀經、禱告或來聚會: He is willing to read Scripture, to pray, or to come to a gathering
這是最多人退卻的階段，因為會被問倒。但要記得：他問問題，代表他在意。回答的原則是: This is where most people retreat, because they get stumped. But remember: his questions mean he cares. The principle for answering is catch the feeling first, then handle the question. What hides under many questions is not an intellectual difficulty but a wounded experience.
分辨這是「知識的問題」還是「心裡的傷」: Discern whether this is a question of knowledge or a wound of the heart
誠實承認自己不懂的部分，一起去找答案: Honestly admit what you do not know, and go looking for the answer together
邀他一起讀一卷福音書（約翰福音或路加福音）: Invite him to read a Gospel with you (John or Luke)
處理具體攔阻：家人反對、拜祖先、時間、罪的捆綁: Deal with the concrete obstacles: family objection, ancestral offerings, time, the grip of sin
問他：你會這樣想，是因為遇過什麼事嗎？: Ask him: did something happen that made you think this way?
去疑問解答庫找一題，先自己讀熟: Find the matching question in the answer library and know it well yourself first
邀他一起讀約翰福音，一天一小段: Invite him to read John with you, a short passage a day
老實跟他說：這題我也不確定，我們一起找答案: Tell him plainly: I am not sure about this one either; let us find the answer together
他親口承認耶穌是主: He confesses with his own mouth that Jesus is Lord
決志不是話術的成功，是聖靈的工作。我們的責任是把福音講清楚，並且勇敢地發出邀請。: A commitment is not the success of a technique; it is the work of the Holy Spirit. Our responsibility is to make the gospel clear and to give the invitation courageously. Many people never come to Christ simply because nobody ever formally asked them.
用五幕結構完整講一次福音: Tell the gospel through once in full, using the five acts
誠實說明信主的代價與福分: Name honestly both the cost of believing and the blessing
發出明確的邀請：「你願意現在接受嗎？」: Give a clear invitation: “would you be willing to receive Him now?”
帶領決志禱告，並立刻約好下一次見面: Lead the prayer of commitment, and fix the next meeting immediately
先禱告，然後約一個能好好談的時間: Pray first, then arrange a time when you can talk properly
把五幕福音先自己讀一遍: Read the five-act gospel through once yourself first
誠實跟他說福分，也說代價: Tell him honestly about the blessing, and about the cost
鼓起勇氣問那一句：你願意現在接受嗎？: Take courage and ask the one question: would you be willing to receive Him now?
受洗，並融入一個群體: Baptised, and settled into a community
決志後的三十天是黃金期也是危險期。一個人若在六週內沒有交到三個教會的朋友，流失的: The thirty days after a commitment are both the golden window and the danger zone. If someone makes no three friends in the church within six weeks, the chance of losing him is very high. So what matters at this stage is not the curriculum but the transplanting of relationships.
決志後四十八小時內第一次跟進: Make the first follow-up within forty-eight hours of the commitment
帶他認識至少三位弟兄姊妹: Introduce him to at least three brothers and sisters
陪他上完慕道班八課: Walk with him through all eight lessons of the Seeker Class
陪他預備受洗見證，出席他的受洗: Help him prepare his baptism testimony, and be there on the day
今天就傳訊息給他，不要等: Send him a message today; do not wait
約好這週介紹一位弟兄姊妹給他: Arrange to introduce one brother or sister to him this week
陪他上慕道班的下一課: Sit with him through the next Seeker Class lesson
問他：關於受洗，你心裡有什麼想法？: Ask him: what are your thoughts about baptism?
生活有改變，能自己靈修: His life is changing and he can keep his own devotions
受洗是起點不是終點。這個階段要把「先生命、再關係、後事工」的次序建造進去，並且完: Baptism is the starting line, not the finish. At this stage the order — life first, then relationships, then ministry — must be built in, and the shift from the old self-centred man to the new selfless man must be completed.
每週一次一對一，持續三個月: One-to-one once a week for three months
教他讀經、禱告、記錄: Teach him to read, to pray, and to record
陪他處理生命中的具體難題: Work through the concrete difficulties of his life with him
示範給他看：帶他一起去關心別人: Show him how: take him along to care for someone else
問他這週靈修讀到什麼: Ask him what he read in his devotions this week
帶他一起去關心另一個人: Take him with you to care for another person
陪他處理他現在最卡住的那件事: Work through the thing he is most stuck on right now
他開始陪伴他自己的一個 2: He has begun walking with a 2 of his own
這是最容易被忽略、卻決定一切的一步。若不繁殖，一切努力只是加法。真正的成功，是他: This is the step most easily overlooked and the one that decides everything. Without reproduction, all the effort is only addition. Real success is that he no longer needs you and has begun a list of his own.
把你會的教給他，然後讓他去做: Teach him what you know, and then let him do it
在旁邊支持，但不代替他做: Support from the side, but do not do it for him
為他的屬靈兒女一同禱告: Pray together for his spiritual children
問他：你心裡有沒有想帶的人？: Ask him: is there someone on your heart you would like to lead?
陪他寫下他的第一張名單（三個名字）: Sit with him as he writes his first list (three names)
讓他講一次福音給你聽，你只聽不改: Have him tell you the gospel once; only listen, do not correct
我記錄他，是為了更好地愛他，不是為了管理他。: I keep a record of him in order to love him better, not to manage him.
我絕不把他的私事告訴不相干的人，包括在代禱時。: I will never tell his private business to anyone with no part in it, not even in prayer requests.
我尊重他的自由，他有權利說不，也有權利慢慢來。: I respect his freedom. He has the right to say no, and the right to take his time.
我不把人數當成績。一個靈魂比一百個數字寶貴。: I will not treat numbers as results. One soul is worth more than a hundred figures.
我知道使人重生的是聖靈，不是我。我只負責忠心。: I know it is the Holy Spirit who gives new birth, not me. My part is only to be faithful.
為配偶得救: For a spouse to be saved
主啊，祢知道我心裡最深的掛念。我把我的另一半交在祢手中。 求祢挪去他心裡的攔阻，:
Lord, You know the deepest concern of my heart. I place the one I married into Your hands.
Take away what stands in the way inside him; soften the hardness that the years have laid down. Send someone to his side who will speak to him in words he can understand.
Lord, change me first. Do not let me substitute nagging for love, or comparison for acceptance. Let him see the gentleness of Christ in me before anything else.
I do not know how long the wait will be, but I am willing to wait. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.

Father, thank You for placing me in this family.
I come before You for my parents. They raised me all my life, and I have still not given them the best thing of all. Have mercy on them, and as their years grow long, open the eyes of their hearts.
Give me wisdom to know when to speak and when to be quiet. Let my devotion to them show them first that this God is real.
Lord, there is not much time. Hasten Your work. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
主啊，這孩子本來就是祢賜的。 我把他交還給祢。求祢保守他不走偏路，在他心裡放下對:
Lord, this child was Your gift in the first place.
I hand him back to You. Keep him from wandering off the road; plant a longing for You in his heart; and when his need is greatest, bring back to his mind the words he heard as a child.
Make me a parent he is willing to come close to — not pressing him with authority, but drawing him with a life.
Lord, take hold of him Yourself. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
天父，我為我的家人來到祢面前。 我們之間有太多陳年的心結，有些話說了會傷，不說又:
Father, I come before You for my family.
There are too many old knots between us. Some things wound if said and keep us apart if unsaid. Heal the bitterness in me first, and let me be the one to step across.
Prepare the right moment, and let the gospel come into their hearts naturally, through a meal or a visit.
In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
為同事得救: For a colleague to be saved
主啊，祢把我放在這間公司不是偶然的。 求祢讓我在工作上作一個值得信任的人，讓我的:
Lord, it was no accident that You placed me in this company.
Make me someone who can be trusted at work, and let my honesty and my calm be a witness that needs no words.
I pray especially for [name]. Lift the weight from his heart, give me an opening to speak, and give me the right words.
In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
為主管與同業: For managers and those in my trade

Father, give me a heart that submits without flattering and is upright without pride.
I pray for my manager. Bless his family and his health. However he treats me, let me return good for it.
Make me salt and light in my workplace — not by eloquence, but by a life. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
主啊，我們認識這麼多年，我卻一直沒能把最重要的事告訴他。 求祢赦免我的膽怯。求祢:

Forgive my cowardice. Prepare his heart, and prepare my mouth.
Let our friendship not turn awkward because of faith, but grow deeper because of it. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
天父，謝謝祢把這些人放在我身邊。 求祢讓我成為一個好鄰舍——記得他們的名字，在他:
Father, thank You for placing these people around me.
Make me a good neighbour — one who remembers their names and actually turns up when they are in need.
Through the small things of ordinary days, let them see the likeness of Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
主耶穌，祢在世上的時候醫治了許多人，祢的心腸沒有改變。 我為【某某】的身體禱告，:
Lord Jesus, when You walked on earth You healed many, and Your heart has not changed.
I pray for [name]'s body. Touch him Yourself, ease his pain, give him settled sleep, and strengthen the family caring for him.

天父，祢是安慰人的神。 我為正在失去至親的【某某】禱告。求祢不用道理安慰他，用祢:
Father, You are the God who comforts.
I pray for [name], who is losing someone dear. Do not comfort him with explanations; hold him with Your presence.
In the darkest of the night, let him know there is a hand that has never let go. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
主啊，祢知道他現在的難處。 求祢開路，賜下合適的工作與供應；也求祢在等待的日子裡:
Lord, You know the strait he is in.
Open a way; provide the right work and the supply he needs. And through the days of waiting, guard his dignity and his hope.
Show me what I can actually do to help, rather than only saying pleasant things. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
天父，求祢憐憫這個家。 求祢先軟化兩顆剛硬的心，讓他們願意停下爭辯，開始聽對方說:
Father, have mercy on this home.
Soften the two hard hearts first, so that they are willing to stop arguing and begin to hear each other.
Give them the power to forgive — the thing people cannot do and You can. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
為憂鬱與失眠的人: For those with depression and sleeplessness
主啊，他很累了。 求祢賜他今晚一夜好眠，賜他明天早上一點點力氣。求祢除去他心裡那:
Lord, he is very tired.
Give him one night of good sleep tonight, and a little strength for tomorrow morning. Take away the voice inside that condemns him.

主耶穌，祢說祢來是要釋放被擄的。 我奉祢的名為【某某】禱告，求祢斷開那些綑綁他的:
Lord Jesus, You said You came to set the captives free.
In Your name I pray for [name]. Break the chains that bind him, and give him a new will and new desires.
Provide a community to hold him up, so that he does not have to fight alone. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
主啊，我已經為他禱告很久了，看不出什麼改變。 求祢除掉他的石心，賜他肉心。求祢用:

Take away his heart of stone and give him a heart of flesh. Do it Your way, not mine.

天父，我感覺祢正在他心裡動工。 求祢預備那個時刻，也預備我的口。不讓我急躁催逼，:
Father, I sense that You are at work in his heart.

為初信者站立得穩: For a new believer to stand firm
主啊，謝謝祢，他信了。 求祢保守他這株剛發芽的苗，抵擋隨之而來的攪擾與試探。 求:
Lord, thank You — he has believed.
Guard this newly sprouted shoot against the disturbance and testing that will follow.
Within six weeks, give him three genuine spiritual friends. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
天父，這是一個公開歸屬祢的日子。 求祢賜他勇氣面對家人的眼光，賜他清楚的見證，賜:
Father, this is a day of belonging to You in the open.
Give him courage under the gaze of his family, give him a clear testimony, and give him a glad heart.
Make this day the anchor of his life. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
主啊，在我去愛人之前，求祢先充滿我。 我承認我常常想靠自己的口才、自己的方法。求:
Lord, before I go out to love anyone, fill me first.
I admit I often want to rely on my own eloquence and my own methods. Take away my self, and let Jesus live in me.
Today, let me bear the fruit of the Spirit towards [name] — not me trying hard to be good, but You living within me.
Let Jesus reign, and let Jesus receive all the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
灰心時的禱告: A prayer for when heart fails
主啊，我有點撐不住了。 我看不見果效，也懷疑自己是不是做錯了什麼。求祢提醒我：我:
Lord, I am not sure I can hold up much longer.
I see no results, and I wonder whether I have done something wrong. Remind me: I planted, Apollos watered, but You gave the increase.
Give me back my joy, and let me do this for You alone and not for the outcome.
I am willing to go on being faithful. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray. Amen.
愛是恆久忍耐，又有恩慈。: Love is patient and is kind.
你們要靠主常常喜樂。我再說，你們要喜樂。: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, rejoice!
弟兄們哪，你們要忍耐，直到主來。: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord.
並要以恩慈相待，存憐憫的心。: And be kind to one another, tender hearted.
有了機會就當向眾人行善。: As we have opportunity, let's do what is good toward all men.
人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心。: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.
我心裡柔和謙卑，你們當負我的軛，學我的樣式。: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart.
人不制伏自己的心，好像毀壞的城邑沒有牆垣。: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.

今天為他做一件他不知道是你做的事。: Today, do something for him that he will never know you did.
喜樂不靠環境，靠與主同在。環境給的是快樂，主給的是喜樂。: Joy does not rest on circumstances but on being with the Lord. Circumstances give happiness; the Lord gives joy.
今天跟他分享一件讓你感謝的小事。: Today, share with him one small thing you are thankful for.
和平不是沒有衝突，是在衝突裡不失去裡面的安穩。無己的人不需要贏，所以能和平。: Peace is not the absence of conflict but keeping your inner steadiness within it. The selfless do not need to win, and so they can be at peace.
今天有一次可以爭的機會，選擇不爭。: Today, when a chance to contend comes, choose not to.
忍耐是把時間交給神。你已經等了很久，那是因為神看見的比你長遠。: Patience is handing the timing to God. You have waited a long while because God sees further than you do.
今天不催他任何事，只是問候他。: Today, press him for nothing at all — simply ask how he is.
恩慈是在他不值得的時候仍然待他好。那正是神待我們的方式。: Kindness is treating him well when he does not deserve it. That is exactly how God treats us.
今天說一句肯定他的話，具體到一件事。: Today, say one affirming thing to him, about one specific matter.
良善是即使沒有人看見也照樣做對的事。良善是無己最安靜的樣子。: Goodness is doing the right thing when nobody is watching. Goodness is selflessness at its quietest.
今天做一件沒有人會知道的好事。: Today, do one good thing that nobody will ever know about.
信實是說到做到。在一個人人失信的世代，準時與守約本身就是見證。: Faithfulness is doing what you said. In an age when everyone breaks their word, being on time and keeping an appointment is itself a witness.
今天把一件答應過他卻沒做的事完成。: Today, finish something you promised him and never did.

今天怎麼樣？我一早就想到你。 昨天你做的那個決定，是你一生最重要的一件事，我為你:

No elegant phrasing, no kneeling. You can do it driving, washing dishes, or before you sleep. Just four things: thank You, I am sorry, please help so-and-so, and my own needs.
I will pray once for you to hear, and then it is your turn. One sentence is enough.

I have brought you a Bible.
We will begin with John, a short passage a day, and skip whatever you cannot understand.
Ask three questions each day: what does this say God is like? What does it say man is like? What am I to do today?
(Read the first passage through with him there and then.)

(Arrange with those three beforehand: ask them to come over, greet him, and remember his name.)

Has anything got stuck these three weeks? Has anyone at home said something?

Stop sending material; ask instead, “how have you been?” and then actually wait for him. If there is still no reply, pray for him quietly and wait for the next natural opening — a birthday, an illness, a change of job. Each of these is a moment when the door opens again.

What you can do now is make contact again — but say nothing spiritual, just arrange a meal. Once the relationship is rejoined, the door will open again.

他信了別的宗教，還很虔誠。: He has taken up another religion, and is devout in it.

人吃那果子，不是因為肚子餓。是因為想坐上那個位子。這就是驕傲：離開人的本位，抓住: We ate that fruit not because we were hungry, but because we wanted that seat. This is pride: leaving our own place as creatures, seizing the authority of God, wanting to take his place.
